LESSON: MONEY

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Measurements
Topic 3.7: Money
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Money, part of Measurements in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we use money in daily activities? 2. How is mobile money transactions used in real life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. work out profit and loss in real life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. calculate the percentage profit and loss in different situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. calculate discount and percentage discount of different goods and services,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. calculate commission and percentage commission in real life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. interpret bills at home,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

F. prepare bills in real life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

G. work out postal charges in real life situations,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

H. identify mobile money services for different transactions,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Money in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. work out profit and loss in real life situations,

   Money helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. calculate the percentage profit and loss in different situations,

   Money helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. calculate discount and percentage discount of different goods and services,

   Money helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. calculate commission and percentage commission in real life situations,

   Money helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. interpret bills at home,

   Money helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

F. prepare bills in real life situations,

   Money helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

G. work out postal charges in real life situations,

   Money helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

H. identify mobile money services for different transactions,

   Money helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

I. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Role play shopping and selling activities involving profit, loss, discount and commission. Create a conducive environment and adequate space for learners with mobility difficulties as they role play. Ensure safety for all learners.

2. Work out profit and loss involving different activities and settings in purposive groups/pairs. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional part of the body or assistive digital devices as they perform the task.

3. Work out percentage profit/loss from the role play activities. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Role play shopping and selling activities involving profit, loss, discount and commission. Create a conducive environment and adequate space for learners with mobility difficulties as they role play. Ensure safety for all learners.
2. Work out profit and loss involving different activities and settings in purposive groups/pairs. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional part of the body or assistive digital devices as they perform the task.
3. Work out percentage profit/loss from the role play activities. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Money together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner works out discounts, commissions and mobile money as well as postal

charges and bills.

● Communication and collaboration: as the learner role plays on negotiating for discounts and commissions.

● Citizenship: as the learner works out discounts, commissions and mobile money in Kenyan currency.

● Self-efficacy: as the learner role plays on negotiating for discounts and commissions.

Values

● Patriotism: as the learner role plays and works out paying bills in Kenyan currency.

● Integrity: as the learner pays bills and appreciates use of money.

● Decision making: as the learner uses money in paying bills and postal charges.

● Pre-Technical Studies: as the learner works out bills, discounts, commissions and postal charges.

● Languages: as the learner gathers information on postal services and charges.
